The density can be calculated using the formula:

\[
\text{Density} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}}
\]

Given:
- Mass of Aluminum atom = 26.982 g/mol
- Number of atoms = 500
- Volume = 8745.5037 Å³

First, convert the volume from cubic angstroms to cubic centimeters:

\[
1 \, \text{Å}^3 = 10^{-24} \, \text{cm}^3
\]

\[
\text{Volume in cm}^3 = 8745.5037 \times 10^{-24} \, \text{cm}^3
\]

Next, calculate the mass of the system in grams:

\[
\text{Mass} = \frac{500 \, \text{atoms} \times 26.982 \, \text{g/mol}}{6.022 \times 10^{23} \, \text{atoms/mol}}
\]

Finally, calculate the density:

\[
\text{Density} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume in cm}^3}
\]

Let's perform these calculations.
